purpose: Check whether each agent can deliver the complete page-count proof with 300 seconds and one-call delivery

page-count.request: Write proof steps for the fixed Lean page-count theorem. For example, eleven items at five per page need three pages. Read all claim parts: the invalid-input result, valid-input bounds and this example. The theorem starts without a proof. Keep the Rust source, Lean model, theorem, assumptions, package settings and proof markers unchanged. Use fr to check your tactics. Once a check passes, deliver with one fr proof save call that adds --deliver change.patch: it saves the proof, runs the supplied package check and writes change.patch. Then finish. The Lean files use prelude, which turns off the automatic Init library import; keep the imports unchanged. This proves the mathematical model; the connection to Rust execution remains unproved.

decision_if_prediction_met: Each agent delivered at least one accepted complete proof within 300 seconds. Record the fr actions that contributed; M3 still needs its remaining language and numeric cases.
decision_if_prediction_fails: Inspect where the time went (replies, tools, delivery) and the first unresolved proof step before choosing another change.
publication: Patches and reviewed summaries only; native records, prompts, drafts, snapshots and account data stay local
